summary: WebSocket stream goes silent mid-generation after worker preempt; client observes half-open socket
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports WebSocket-based chat sessions enter a silent state approximately 20-45s into long-generation responses. The server continues to report the worker as alive for a short time, but no bytes are observed at the client; the TCP connection eventually half-closes and the client must reconnect.

Impact: Affects NoteDock Labs (dedicated) for interactive editor feature; ~12% of long-chat sessions (>800 tokens) in us-east-1 experienced a stall in the 48-hour window. Users see a frozen spinner and must refresh or reconnect. No token loss is consistently reproducible but session continuity is disrupted.

Environment: prod, dedicated pool (dp-nd-01) in us-east-1. Traffic routed through ALB -> websocket-proxy fleet -> gateway -> serving-runtime workers. Customers are using WebSocket with incremental event frames (application/json). Many client connections are behind corporate NATs with TCP keepalive enabled.

Observed behavior: mid-generation silence (no SSE/WebSocket frames) for 20-45s, then client receives FIN from upstream or TCP resets after long idle. Server logs sometimes show worker preempt/eviction for the request's worker due to a short-lived eviction event (node maintenance/autoscaler). We see a pattern where the proxy keeps the socket open while the worker has been reassigned; the proxy's half-open behavior results in no application-level error until TCP times out.

Expected behavior: When a worker handling an active streaming request is preempted/evicted, the platform should either: a) graceful failover the stream to a fallback worker with resume support, or b) promptly signal an application-level error over the WebSocket so client can reconnect and resume. Users should not see long silent intervals without an error or reconnect suggestion.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated account in us-east-1 (NoteDock Labs test tenant).
2) Open a WebSocket chat session that triggers a long generation (>800 tokens).
3) While generation is in-flight, trigger a worker preempt by forcing a short restart (internal test: drain one serving node) or cause autoscaler to reassign (simulate load spike).
4) Observe client for silent period and eventual FIN/RESET without an application-level error message.
logs: [2026-02-28T14:25:00Z] websocket-proxy-12: conn_id=abc123 TCP_FIN from upstream=true client_seen_idle=46s
investigation: SRE confirmed worker eviction window coincides with silent period. Proxy keeps TCP session in established state while gateway detects worker disconnect but does not immediately return a WebSocket-level CLOSE frame. Packet captures show no RST from worker until the eviction completes; however, proxy's TCP persist settings and ALB idle timeout are allowing a long half-open interval. Reproducible in internal test cluster when we simulate scheduled preemptions and set the same tcp_keepalive and ALB idle-timeout values as customer's environment.
hypothesis: 1) Worker preempt leads to an internal handoff where gateway transitions connection; proxy and ALB TCP timeouts are longer than application-level detection, producing silent window.

2) Under high token generation, KV cache misses increase latency and extend time-to-detect worker loss, pushing the silent window past client-side keepalive intervals, so the client only sees a socket-level timeout later.
3) Proxy's current behavior does not emit a WebSocket CLOSE or error frame on upstream worker disconnect during streaming; instead it waits on TCP semantics (causing user-visible stall).

next_steps: 1) Deploy PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821 to canary in dedicated pool and run 72h soak with NoteDock traffic replication.
2) Adjust websocket-proxy TCP keepalive and ALB idle timeout defaults for dedicated pools to reduce half-open window (rollback plan in runbook).
3) Add an application-level close/error emission in gateway when worker disconnects mid-stream (server-side fix).
4) Provide customer with client SDK patch notes and recommended reconnection/resume strategy as interim workaround.
5) Postmortem and follow-up: evaluate whether autoscaler eviction cadence or KV-cache warmup profiles can be tuned to reduce mid-gen evictions.
resolution: Triage ongoing; temporary mitigation (proxy keepalive/ALB adjustments) reduced impact in canary. Server-side fix PR created; schedule and verification in progress. Customer notified and given client-side reconnect guidance.
